sections.content: How many people are "arts officers, producers and directors"?

74,755 people

were counted on the census as "arts officers, producers and directors" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Arts officers, producers and directors assume creative, financial and organisational responsibilities in the production and direction of television and radio programmes, films, stage presentations, content for other media, and the promotion and exhibition of other creative activities.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 30 to 34 years. Of the whole working population 12% were aged 30 to 34 years. For people working as "arts officers, producers and directors", 17.2% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "arts officers, producers and directors" was 16 to 19 years.

Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "arts officers, producers and directors" included:

  • biochemists and biomedical scientists
  • brokers
  • clothing, fashion and accessories designers

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "arts officers, producers and directors" there were more men than women (58.2% compared with 41.8%).

This means "arts officers, producers and directors" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "culture, media and sports occupations".

Men made up 58.2% and women made up 41.8% of "arts officers, producers and directors"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "arts officers, producers and directors" included:

  • natural and social science professionals (other)
  • stock control clerks and assistants
  • specialist medical practitioners

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "arts officers, producers and directors" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

The percentage of men and women who are "arts officers, producers and directors" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "arts officers, producers and directors", 8.4% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (76.5% compared with 23.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (50.2%) than self-employed (49.8%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Hackney, this is in the same region of London.
